To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Zn(2)Cys(6) binuclear cluster protein PPR1, as well as its relative GAL4, recognizes DNA sequences that include the conserved palindromic sequence CGG, but that the number of base pairs separating the CGG triplets differs between the proteins.
GAL4 and PRR1 recognize DNA sequences with CGG half sites separated by 11 and 6 bp, respectively.
GAL4 and a relative, PPR1 recognize DNA sequences with palindromic half sites separated by 11 bp for GAL4 and by 6 bp for PPR1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the Zn2 Cys2 binuclear cluster proteins GAL4 and PRR1 recognize specific DNA sequences and how these two proteins differ from each other in this regard.
how Zn2 Cys2 binuclear cluster proteins recognize DNA, a question of broad interest because these proteins play important roles in gene regulation.
how the GAL4 and PRR1 proteins bind to DNA and how this binding is regulated by the presence of other proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GAL4 and PRR1 bind DNA with the same affinity to the CGG half sites but with different affinities to the intervening DNA.
GAL4 and PRR1 are both Zn(2)-Cys6 binuclear clusters with a preference for palindromic DNA sequences.
GAL4 and PRR1 recognize DNA in a similar fashion, except that PRR1 recognizes a shorter sequence, 12 bp rather than 17 bp for GAL4.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DNA sequence preferences of the Zn2 Cys 6 binuclear cluster transcription factors are dictated by the number of CGG half sites present in the site and the spacing between them.

Zn2 Cys2 binuclear cluster proteins recognize DNA sequences by means of two different strategies: one that is sensitive to the identities of the central 6 bp of the 12-bp site and another that is not sensitive.
GAL4 and P PR1 have similar, but not identical, sequence preferences, and that the GAL4-D NA complex structure is consistent with the observed sequence preferences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GAL4 and PRR1 DNA binding sites have been overestimated.

the Zn2 Cys 6 binuclear cluster protein GAL4 and the related protein PPR1 recognize their cognate sequences with high affinity and specificity by using different subsets of the DNA recognition surface.
GAL4 and PRR1 are both sequence specific, but they recognize different sequences.
